title: Striking the Benefit That Properly Stands on a Line Put Right
content:
When a line under one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is put right, the benefit that properly stands on it is struck according to the benefit category the line falls in.

## The rule

**Where the line put right falls in a benefit category carrying a flat allowance**, the benefit that properly stands is the lesser of the benefit basis and that flat allowance.

**Where the line put right is a routine eye examination**, the benefit that properly stands is the benefit basis less the routine eye examination copayment the rider held carries.

**Otherwise**, the coinsurance percentage the line's benefit category carries is taken on the benefit basis and rounded to the nearest cent.

## Input, judgement, output

| The line put right | The benefit basis | The benefit that properly stands |
|---|---|---|
| A set of eyeglass frames, the rider's frame allowance being 175.00 USD | 260.00 USD | 175.00 USD, the lesser of the two |
| A set of eyeglass frames, the rider's frame allowance being 175.00 USD | 140.00 USD | 140.00 USD, the lesser of the two |
| A routine eye examination, the rider's routine eye examination copayment being 10.00 USD | 85.00 USD | 75.00 USD |
| A routine eye examination, the rider's routine eye examination copayment being 0.00 USD | 85.00 USD | 85.00 USD |
| Major restorative dental care, the rider's share for it being 60 per cent | 900.00 USD | 540.00 USD |
| Dentures, the rider's share for them being 50 per cent | 1200.00 USD | 600.00 USD |

Every figure in the table is a hypothetical input.

## Note on the order of the three cases

A line falling in a benefit category that carries a flat allowance is settled by the first case, whatever coinsurance percentage the rider may carry elsewhere; a routine eye examination, which carries no flat allowance, is settled by the second; and only a line answering to neither is settled by taking the coinsurance percentage on the benefit basis. Where the third case governs, the rounding to the nearest cent is done once the percentage has been taken.
